QuestionStmt.S: The function defined by $f(x) = \frac{2x+3}{3x+4}, x \neq -\frac{4}{3}$ is

Solution.S:
One-one: Assume $f(x_1) = f(x_2)$.

$$\frac{2x_1+3}{3x_1+4} = \frac{2x_2+3}{3x_2+4}$$

Cross-multiplying: $(2x_1+3)(3x_2+4) = (2x_2+3)(3x_1+4)$

Expanding: $6x_1x_2 + 8x_1 + 9x_2 + 12 = 6x_1x_2 + 8x_2 + 9x_1 + 12$

Cancel $6x_1x_2$ and $12$: $8x_1 + 9x_2 = 8x_2 + 9x_1 \Rightarrow 8x_1 - 9x_1 = 8x_2 - 9x_2 \Rightarrow -x_1 = -x_2 \Rightarrow x_1 = x_2$.

Thus $f$ is one-one.

Onto: Let $y = \frac{2x+3}{3x+4}$. Solve for $x$:

$y(3x+4) = 2x+3 \Rightarrow 3xy + 4y = 2x + 3 \Rightarrow 3xy - 2x = 3 - 4y \Rightarrow x(3y - 2) = 3 - 4y \Rightarrow x = \frac{3 - 4y}{3y - 2}$.

$x$ is defined for all $y \neq \frac{2}{3}$. So $f$ is onto for $y \neq \frac{2}{3}$.

Thus the correct option is C: onto for $y \neq \frac{2}{3}$ and one-one.
